_comment: Web-research cost protocol — see omnis docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-30-web-agent-cost-protocol-design.md. Three shapes are the validity floor: lookup (D must pay off), deep multi-turn (A/B must pay off), canary (must FAIL if a variant truncates). `facts`/`forbidden` are scored by scoring.py; `on` is a turn index into answers[].

tasks.prompt: En France, quelle est la durée de validité d'un contrôle technique automobile pour une voiture particulière ?
tasks.notes: Lookup tier: one search away, stable regulation, and French-bound so it also exercises the search-language rule. This is the task V4 (depth-ladder gating) must make cheaper WITHOUT losing the fact. A high fetches count here is itself the defect.

prompts: Sur une DS7 de 2018 la trappe a essence n'est jamais verrouillée, est-ce que c'est normal ?
combien coûte le remplacement de l'actuateur ?
donne moi les références de la pièce neuve et d'occasion.
tasks.notes: Verbatim replay of conversation_fitting-eagle.json — the trace that cost $2.87, of which web_agent was $2.5157 (9.4M prompt / 45k output tokens). GATE CALIBRATED, NOT GUESSED (2026-08-30, 3x --repeat of the untouched baseline, $6.003 total, see tasks-4 report): literal-regex hold rates were actuator 1/3, price-new 2/3, oem 0/3 (5 runs across this task's history have now produced 5 different-or-absent literal OEM numbers: 9820772380 orig. trace, 9810871780/788269092R first verification run, 98285011ZD calib run1, none in calib runs 2-3 — the number never reproduces, so it cannot gate), caveat 3/3. Each concept was then broadened to its SHAPE and re-scored OFFLINE against the 3 captured answer sets (no extra live spend): actuator (/actuateur|actionneur|verrouill|centralis/, engaging with the locking-mechanism concept turn 0 is about) reached 3/3 and stays required. price-new broadened to any price figure reached only 2/3 (run2's web search was down and it reported zero price data at all, honestly) — demoted to required:false. oem's naive 'shape' idea (10-13 alnum chars) is a FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP under this repo's always-re.I matcher — [0-9A-Z] case-folds to any letter, so it matched ordinary words like 'Understood'/'souhaitez'/'Crossback', a bogus 3/3; corrected to a digit-anchored form (10 digits, or 6-9 digits + up to 3 letters) it honestly scores 1/3 (only calib run1's genuine 98285011ZD; runs 2-3 gave no reference at all) — demoted to required:false. The forbidden 'ref-as-fact' rule (flagging 9831776780 stated without a hedge) never got the chance to fire in 3/3 calibration runs (that literal number never recurred) and was DROPPED rather than kept as a shape-based rule: any such rule would share its hedge vocabulary with the now-required `caveat` fact and so could never fire on a run where caveat also holds — which, by construction, is every passing run — making it a dead rule that could not fire. All three calibration runs independently reported their own web-search backend degraded or failed outright ('DuckDuckGo is completely non-functional' / 'les outils de recherche web sont actuellement inopérants') after a burst of 100+ WebSearch calls each — a likely self-inflicted rate-limit from three deep-replay runs back to back, not a property of the model. This is why low-rate facts were demoted to optional rather than dropped outright: they may well be more reliable once that recovers, but the gate must be calibrated to what the baseline actually reproduces, not to what we expect it to reproduce. Ground truth for any surfaced OEM/used-part reference is still NOT independently confirmed by hand — this task measures consistency against a calibrated baseline, not real-world correctness.
